text.en: Meena saw her face upside-down in the back of a shiny spoon. "Why is it inverted?" she asked.

Optics is the branch of physics that deals with light. In reflection from a plane mirror the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and the image is virtual, erect, of the same size and laterally inverted. Spherical mirrors are of two kinds: the concave mirror, which curves inwards, and the convex mirror, which curves outwards.
A concave mirror can form real or virtual images depending on the position of the object, and it is used as a shaving mirror and in headlights. A convex mirror always gives a smaller, virtual, erect image with a wide field of view, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror.
The bending of light when it passes obliquely from one transparent medium to another is refraction. The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is the refractive index, and it has no unit. When light goes from a denser to a rarer medium at an angle beyond the critical angle, total internal reflection occurs, which makes diamonds sparkle and stars twinkle.

problem.en: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 30 degrees to the normal. What is the angle of reflection?

text.en: The law of reflection says i = r.
So the angle of reflection is 30 degrees.

prompt.en: A friend says A convex mirror is used as a shaving mirror. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Shaving mirrors are concave because they magnify the face.
Convex mirrors give a wide, smaller view and are used for vehicle rear-view.

points.en: Total internal reflection needs the critical angle.
